messages:
alex.nguyen: Heads-up — vendor just pinged: our reserved A100 shipment for eu-west1 will be delayed ~3 weeks. They offered an H100 swap at +18% list price or keep A100 with ETA update. Need quick decision: swap, wait, or split pool?
maria.khan: 3 weeks on dedicated pools is rough for customer X. Do we have rough cost delta per-hour for H100 vs A100 with our discounts?
shane: I can run numbers. Quick Q: is the affected pool the 'dedicated-eu-worker-1' (4x A100) or the new burst pool?
alex.nguyen: It's dedicated-eu-worker-1 — currently 4x A100-80GB pinned for invoice tier.
shane: Ok. Rough calc (very rough): list H100 ~ 1.6x A100 raw; after vendor discount + reserved commit we end up ~1.18x cost per-GPU. That's where the +18% came from. Will run the precise hourly with our enterprise pricing and post in 30m.
vendor-bot: @eng-infra Vendor update: H100 units available immediate in eu-west1. A100 ETA revised to 2026-04-12. Swap requires signed amendment; we can provision H100 within 48 hours upon confirmation.
maria.khan: If swap reduces our outage risk for customer X, finance leans toward swap if delta < 25% given SLA penalties. Can engineering quantify perf gains/losses vs our runtime?
shane: Perf note: for our typical sequence lengths (avg 512, batch 8), H100 kernels reduce latency ~20% and increase throughput ~30% on trunk runtime. But inference memory patterns matter: if model is INT8-quantized we might not fully utilize H100 fp16. Need per-model bench.
alex.nguyen: We have two models in that pool: rwd-base-13b (fp16) and rwd-chat-70b (int8). rwd-chat-70b might benefit less. Option: mixed pool 2xH100 + 2xA100 and smart routing. Thoughts?
shane: Mixed pool is viable — runtime supports model->instance hinting. Quick config (pseudo):
```yaml
pools:
  dedicated-eu-worker-1:
    nodes:
      - type: h100-80gb
        count: 2
      - type: a100-80gb
        count: 2
    routing_policy: model_hint
    autoscale: min:2 max:8
```
This gives us H100 for fp16-heavy workloads and A100 for int8. Billing wise you'd be charged per-instance.
maria.khan: OK can you capture delta cost for mixed vs full-swap vs wait? Need monthly TCO + SLA risk line item.
shane: Will do. Also note procurement lead time for A100 could slip further, so waiting has a risk. I'll ping vendor contact for firm commit dates and amendment draft.
sre-oncall: Quick ops note — if we swap, update our capacity radar and alerting thresholds (token throughput per-GPU) — otherwise autoscaler might misjudge. I'll add a small todo to the runbook.
alex.nguyen: Thanks. For immediate next steps: 1) shane posts detailed cost numbers + vendor amendment draft, 2) maria assesses finance risk threshold, 3) sre-oncall prepares runbook change. If we can agree by EOD then we can sign and get H100 within 48h.
maria.khan: I'll aim for EOD. If cost delta < 22% and SLA risk high -> approve.
shane: Posting numbers now: (1) full H100 swap: +18% monthly on committed pool (~$9.2k/mo delta), (2) mixed 2H100/2A100: +9% (~$4.6k/mo), (3) wait: $0 immediate but projected SLA penalty exposure up to $15k for customer X if incident triggers. Draft amendment link: https://vendor.example.com/amend/ABC-123
alex.nguyen: Nice, thanks. Can someone +1 for mixed approach so I can tell vendor to prepare an amendment for mixed pool?
sre-oncall: +1 :thumbsup: mixed reduces risk and cost delta looks reasonable.
maria.khan: +1 from finance for mixed if we confirm routing works with minimal code changes.
shane: I'll verify routing tomorrow morning with a quick canary (bench tests). If green, I'll sign off on engineering side and ask vendor to prepare amendment.
alex.nguyen: Great — I'll update customer X success thread and schedule a 15m sync if needed. Closing loop here once vendor confirms amendment readiness. :white_check_mark:
